does: Whisks flour with eggs and milk into a smooth, thin, lump-free batter, by working the liquid into the flour a little at a time.
how: Put the flour and salt in a bowl and make a well in the middle.
Break the eggs into the well and whisk them, drawing in flour from the sides.
Add the milk a little at a time, whisking, until the batter is smooth and pours like thin cream.
Leave it to stand while the oven and the fat heat.

cues.text: A smooth, shiny batter with no lumps, that runs off the whisk in a ribbon that sinks at once.
No grit of dry flour against the side of the bowl.

mistakes.mistake: Tipping in all the milk at the start, so that the flour forms lumps that never whisk out.
mistakes.fix: Make a thick paste first and thin it slowly.

mistakes.mistake: A batter that is too thick, so that it bakes heavy.
mistakes.fix: Thin it with a little more milk.

variant_of.differs: Flour is drawn into the eggs and milk a little at a time to make a smooth batter, rather than eggs or cream beaten on their own.
